A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mirror-map learning research, with common authors, methods, and experiments despite substantial revision. All 17 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original AMPO experiments on Basic Control and MinAtar environments, learned mirror maps, and cross-environment transfer results in Section 5 and Appendix B.3.

after.justification: v2 reports original Grid-World experiments and diagnostics, revised non-tabular learning curves, and transfer evaluations in Section 4, Figures 2–3, and Table 1.

M1.justification: The learning objective changes from average return throughout training in v1 Section 4.2 to final-policy value in v2 Equation (7). v2 also introduces tabular PMD with a monotone neural parameterization of the inverse potential and multitask, rank-based OpenAI-ES, alongside the retained piecewise-potential and sep-CMA approach for AMPO.

E1.justification: v2 adds training over a distribution of Grid-World tasks and evaluation on five held-out configurations and 256 randomly sampled configurations. It removes Breakout from the non-tabular benchmark and transfer comparisons, retaining Acrobot, CartPole, Asterix, Freeway, and SpaceInvaders.

E2.justification: The non-tabular comparison replaces greedy-exp, the doubled-step-size negative-entropy baseline in v1 Figure 2, with the ℓ2 mirror map in v2 Figure 3. Negative entropy is retained and also becomes an explicit comparator in the transfer table, where v1 compared only learned maps.

E3.justification: Non-tabular hyperparameter tuning changes from per-environment to per-suite settings. For example, BCS parallel environments change from 10/16 to 4, and all discount factors become 0.99. v2 also introduces a Grid-World protocol using grid search, 128 PMD iterations, and 2^18 environment steps. These are reported setting changes, not merely additional disclosure.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial diagnostics connecting value trajectories to exact Q-estimation errors and distances between successive policies in Grid-World. Transfer analysis now assesses performance against negative entropy. The earlier greedy-exp comparison testing whether increased greediness or step size explains performance is removed.

E5.justification: Non-tabular figure captions report 100 realizations in v2 instead of 20 in v1. v2 additionally specifies 256 runs for Grid-World plots and 100 runs for transfer results. Learning curves retain mean and standard-error reporting; no new significance-testing or confidence-interval procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds Grid-World results and replaces the non-tabular curves and transfer scores. Acrobot changes from favoring negative entropy over the learned map in v1 to a higher final value for the learned map in v2. The Asterix self-transfer entry changes from 14.43 in v1 Table 2 to 30.22 in v2 Table 1. Revised objectives, settings, and final-policy reporting prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v1's AMPO convergence theorem and approximation, concentrability, and distribution-mismatch assumptions are replaced by tabular inexact-PMD bounds and new proofs in v2 Theorem 2.2 and Appendix B. The invariance and policy-derivative results and proofs are removed, while the parameter-validity argument is retained. As printed, the new convergence formulas omit the averaging factor on the value sum.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from learning effective neural-policy AMPO mirror maps to investigating both tabular and non-tabular PMD. v2 adds headline claims that estimation error poorly predicts performance and that small policy updates accompany fewer performance dips. Its abstract also strengthens potential transferability into a claim of good generalization.

C2.justification: v2 introduces interpretations linking policy-update size to stability and explaining why estimation-error bounds do not rank empirical performance well. It removes v1's effective-horizon explanation for learned-map behavior and its discussion of Breakout's weak transfer. The warning about insufficient exploration remains, and v2 explicitly limits direct theoretical diagnostics to the tabular setting.

D1.justification: v2 adds tabular implementation details, four-A40/12-hour resource reporting, and ES population, generation, and noise settings in Appendix C. It drops several earlier hyperparameters, explicit parameter-normalization instructions, and the future code-release statement. The main-text positive-orthant parameter domain also conflicts with the simplex domain retained in Appendix A.2, reducing reproducibility clarity.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting Grid-World, GAE, and future evaluation directions, including Oh et al., Chevalier-Boisvert et al., Schulman et al. (2016), and Osband et al.; it removes Laidlaw et al. The established PMD positioning largely remains, with increased emphasis on Xiao's tabular analysis. Jackson's venue/year update concerns the same cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution narrative, experimental discussion, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Preliminaries, methodology, and experiments are reorganized around tabular and non-tabular settings, and the appendices are rebuilt around different proofs and training details. The title changes from 'Meta-learning the mirror map in policy mirror descent' to 'Learning mirror maps in policy mirror descent.'

P2.justification: v2 retains only the parameterization panel from v1 Figure 1, adds the Grid-World diagnostic figure, and redraws the non-tabular comparison. The transfer heatmap and appendix raw/normalized tables become a colored main-text table with a negative-entropy row. The three-action illustration and algorithm box disappear, and the document adopts substantially different typography and layout.

improvement.justification: The held-out Grid-World diagnostics, ℓ2 comparisons, and explicit transfer baseline strengthen evidence for claims that v1 supported mainly through benchmark curves. However, v2 removes Breakout and useful reproducibility details while introducing mathematical inconsistencies: Equation (4) and Theorem B.4 lack the value-sum averaging factor, and the main-text parameter domain conflicts with Appendix A.2. These problems affect the theoretical and implementation basis of the expanded claims. The substantial empirical benefits and losses in correctness and clarity leave the net quality change uncertain.
